transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is openly challenging New York's Chuck Schumer
for the role of Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress.
Van Hollen has the support of fellow progressives,
while Schumer holds sway over moderate Democrats.
Here's NPR's Luke Garrett.
>> Coming off a historic midterm election victory in the Senate,
Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York is facing a challenge for leadership.
In a statement Thursday, Senator Van Hollen said Americans called for change at the ballot box,
and that means new leadership in the Senate.
Senator-elect Abdul Sayed told NPR he supports Van Hollen,
citing his "righteous fights" against the Trump administration.
Schumer does maintain support within his caucus.
On Thursday, Senator Angus King, an independent from Maine who votes with Democrats,
endorsed Schumer and called him the architect of the most successful election in modern history.
Democratic Senate leadership elections are set for early December.
Luke Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
>> The string of Democratic victories in last week's midterm elections
has extended to the Kansas governor's office.
Kansas voters have chosen Democratic State Senator Cindy Holsher
to succeed outgoing Democratic Governor Laura Kelly.
The influential ADI chipmaker, Invidia, says Chief Financial Officer Collette Kress,
has agreed to be the company's interim CEO.
Following Thursday's resignation of founder Jensen Huang
after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy,
Kevin Roos is a co-host of NPR's Machine Gods podcast.
>> Well, I think the first thing that she has to do is just to keep people calm, right?
Customers, employees, investors, people are already worried about, you know,
momentum shifting to AMD or another rival.
The second would be the money.
I mean, Invidia has been acting as a kind of bank for the entire AI industry.
It has deals with all of the biggest AI labs,
including hundreds of billions of dollars of commitments
and circular financing deals.
And Collette Kress signed off on many of those deals,
but she has to now decide whether to keep writing the checks.
And then I just think she's going to have a lot of investigations to deal with.
There's going to be this board investigation, an FBI inquiry.
>> The U.S. serviceman arrested in the U.K. on suspicion of espionage
as an Army Lieutenant Colonel.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports he was caught in a sting by British authorities.
>> The 41-year-old Army Lieutenant Colonel,
currently being held by U.K. Metropolitan Police,
has served nearly 20 years and had deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan.
A U.S. Army counterintelligence command spokesman confirms to NPR
that the suspect was caught in a sting,
where he didn't know he was speaking to British agents.
U.K. authorities allege he was attempting to share sensitive information with Russia.
He's currently being held in London and will be charged early next week
and then transferred to American custody
and charged under the Uniform Code of Military Justice.
In recent weeks, U.S. bases in the U.K. have been on high alert for possible attacks linked to the war in Iran.
But British authorities say this case is not related.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
>> This is NPR.
White House envoy Steve Whitkoff and Jared Kushner
are on their way to meet with Ukraine's president.
The two are to meet with Volodymyr Solinsky in Dublin
after briefing Russian leader Volodymyr Putin at the Kremlin
on this week's U.S.-led peace talks in Abu Dhabi.
Whitkoff has confirmed that Putin agreed to allow European representatives
to join the next round.
Microsoft got hit with a massive outage across its office software suite today.
Thousands of users were unable to access e-mail and messaging,
as NPR's Catherine Welch reports.
>> The outage tracker down detector shows reports suddenly spiked
at nearly 130,000 users at around 1 p.m. Eastern,
with thousands more coming in as the day went on.
The outage kept users from accessing e-mail through Outlook
or sending message over Teams
and affected other apps in the Microsoft office suite.
It's not clear what prompted the outage, but in updates on social media,
Microsoft said it was aware that users were encountering issues
in "multiple connection methods" in the Americas.
We should note Microsoft is a financial supporter of NPR.
The company has been providing updates on social media
and said it was trying several fixes.
Catherine Welch, NPR News.
>> Asian shares mixed in Friday trading.
The markets in Tokyo, Shanghai, and Taiwan are advancing.
Taiwan's benchmark is up.
1.6% stocks elsewhere in the region declining
following modest losses Thursday on Wall Street.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.

topics.text: Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen challenges Chuck Schumer for Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress
Democrat Cindy Holsher wins Kansas governor's race to succeed Laura Kelly
Nvidia names CFO Colette Kress interim CEO after Jensen Huang's resignation over extramarital affair reports
U.S. Army Lieutenant Colonel arrested in U.K. on suspicion of espionage for Russia in British sting
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner travel to Dublin to meet Ukraine's President Zelensky after Putin talks
Microsoft Outlook, Teams, and Office suite suffer major outage affecting thousands of users in the Americas
Asian stock markets mixed in Friday trading, with Taiwan's benchmark rising 1.6%
